moduleTitle: Lesson 9 - Export and Create the TestCase
learningObjectives: Distinguish consuming a buffer in a request from capturing a response value.
Build an independent order verification flow.
Scope dynamic month boundaries and numerical assertions to the contract.

elements.text: Assume an authorized disposable sandbox allows reading an address, creating an order and retrieving it by identifier. Configure messages and authentication from that contract, export through API TestCase, inspect references and define expected outcomes. Original DemoWebShop order operations, prices and exercise data were not verified.

Independent guidance: test success and fault behavior; observed server values can identify existing resources but do not alone establish the correct business result. Authentication is contract-specific, not a universal SOAP statelessness rule.

Add and buffer on a request defaults to Insert with a buffer-reference DefaultValue. The response workflow defaults to Buffer and an element-name DefaultValue. Independent guidance: capture the created identifier before consuming it, and inspect actual Value and ActionMode. Request insertion does not itself capture returned data.

MONTHFIRST and MONTHLAST compute month boundaries using the current date when the base date is empty. Keep all three bracket parameters: {MONTHFIRST[][][yyyy-MM-dd]} or {MONTHLAST[][][yyyy-MM-dd]}. The expression format is explicit rather than a hardcoded calendar date.

Independent warning: appending T01:00:00 excludes the first hour of the month; a T23:59:59 inclusive end can omit subsecond events. Neither string supplies a timezone. Agree on the service timezone and interval semantics; dynamic dates do not automatically guarantee complete coverage. Prefer an explicit boundary contract, often an exclusive next-month start, where the service supports it.

Numeric DataType interprets numbers rather than exact string notation. Choose it for numeric amount assertions; separately define currency, scale, rounding and acceptable tolerance. Numerical equality alone does not prove tax or shipping rules.

Independent flow: configure custom TCP references on supported objects, generate defaults at the needed scope, capture the created identifier, retrieve that resource and verify independently calculated amounts. Inspect list filtering and cleanup if the contract requires a collection lookup.
Prepare messages and map inputs, status/fault assertions and returned identity in a disposable sandbox. Academy Exercise 09a was inaccessible and its solution is not certified.

Run only against an available authorized endpoint or a documented simulation. Inspect affected mappings and all business assertions, including boundary cases. Academy Exercise 09b was inaccessible; no Tosca execution was performed.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing buffer consumption and capture
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming request Add and buffer captures a returned value.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Request defaults to Insert with a reference; response defaults to Buffer.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming dynamic dates imply complete coverage
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Ignoring timezone, the first hour or subsecond end events.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Define interval boundaries from the service contract and test edge cases.

examPitfalls.title: Equating numeric comparison with business correctness
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Accepting equal numbers without validating pricing rules.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Define expected amounts, currency and rounding independently.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does Add and buffer default to for a request ModuleAttribute?
practiceQuiz.hint: The request consumes an input reference.
practiceQuiz.rationale: This differs from response capture using Buffer.

optionExplanations.A: This is the current request default.
optionExplanations.B: A request is not capturing the returned response here.
optionExplanations.D: Attribute creation does not create a new TestCase.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which expression renders the first day of the current month as yyyy-MM-dd and appends the literal time 01:00:00?
practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish first/last and the requested output format.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The expression renders the stated value, but the 01:00 boundary omits the first hour and contains no timezone.

optionExplanations.B: This matches the stated date format and literal time; interval completeness is separate.
optionExplanations.C: A shifted current date is not necessarily the month start.
optionExplanations.D: This uses a different date format.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why choose Numeric for a numerical amount assertion rather than exact string notation?

options.text: Equivalent numerical representations can compare as numbers.
Every API value must be Numeric.

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate number equality from textual spelling.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Numeric interprets numbers; independently verify currency and rounding policy.

optionExplanations.A: This addresses numerical interpretation, not every pricing rule.
optionExplanations.B: Identifiers and text may require other types.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What determines authentication for each operation in an order flow?

options.text: The service contract and chosen security mechanism.
API Scan requires authentication only for POST.
REST rules automatically define SOAP credentials.

practiceQuiz.hint: Do not infer credentials from SOAP alone.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Use the documented security contract for each operation.

optionExplanations.A: This scopes credentials to the actual service.
optionExplanations.B: Method alone does not impose this universal rule.
optionExplanations.D: Different service contracts can use different mechanisms.

quickRecap.value: Inspect contract-configured messages and generated references.
Request Insert consumes a reference; response Buffer captures data.
Capture identity, retrieve resource, assert independent expectations.
Dynamic date expressions still require timezone and interval decisions.
Numeric interpretation plus explicit currency/rounding assertions.
